title: How to do Piana & Toshiki raises
summary: In a garage gym without a calf machine, NH demonstrates two of the three calf movements he will use to add two inches to his calves: "Piana raises" (weighted calf raises off a shallow deficit with a squeeze and slow negative) and "Toshiki raises" (a snatch-grip high-pull-style movement used for momentum into an explosive calf raise). He does them at the end of leg day 2-3 times a week.

claims.claim: NH's goal is to add two inches to his calves, and these are two of the three movements he'll use, chosen because they agree with his body and give a good pump.
You don't need a calf machine: simple movements based on progressive overload can grow calves in a garage gym.

Piana raises (named for Rich Piana): calf raises holding weights (straight bar or dumbbells) off a deficit that is not too steep; the stretch matters less than a hard squeeze/pause at the top and a slow negative.
NH creates the deficit with a block, with plates behind it to touch at the bottom, and prefers a narrow stance with toes pointed out.

Toshiki raises (named for Japanese weightlifter Toshiki Yamamoto): essentially a high pull that doesn't reach the torso, using the momentum of the pull to drive an explosive calf raise with a squeeze at the top.
For Toshiki raises use a wider stance (to complement the narrow-stance Piana raises) and a snatch grip, which NH finds more comfortable and keeps the bar from hitting the belly.
Piana raises are done for 8-12 reps; Toshiki raises, being explosive, for 6-10 reps.
NH does both at the end of leg day, 2-3 times a week.
